enemies.grid_notes: Hird door-ward in the east doorway (elev 1); holds the obvious exit. The opening lesson: the front door is a lie.
First pursuer on Grím's heels, in the yard outside the south hall door [4,5] (elev 0).
Cuts the direct lane to the gate — the central road beside the north storehouse (elev 0).
Bow on the east wall-walk south of the SE stair at [14,6] (elev 3): owns the open yards. His height is also the player's exit — killing him buys BOTH safety and a launch point; the map's best trade.
Gate-ward on the east gate-tower (elev 4) over the S gate passage [13,12]-[14,13]; drops the bar at turn 8 (trigger). Until then the S gate is the cheap exit; after, the wall-drop is the only door.

The hired níð-singer on the dais (elev 2; unnamed by design — a mouth, not a man; the commissioner is the Ch2 question). Chants the verse on loop: aura debuff (player units within 3 tiles, −hit morale sting) and pursuit buff. Faces the steward's high seat, back to the hall — an offered backstab. Downing him stops the chant, not the poem.
The steward's champion, drunk and delighted, mid-yard by the lane brazier at [10,6] (elev 0); fastest pursuer, ignores facing discipline — punishable but relentless.
REINFORCEMENT (turn 3 trigger): wave 1 of the roused hird, entering at the north lane mouth [10,0]. Held off-board until the trigger fires.
REINFORCEMENT (turn 5 trigger): wave 2, through the steward's private west door behind the dais [1,1] — flushes the hall if the player lingers indoors. Held off-board until the trigger fires.
REINFORCEMENT (turn 7 trigger): wave 3, entering at the NE end of the wall-walk [14,1] (elev 3) — retakes the walk; the escape window narrows visibly. Held off-board until the trigger fires.

neutrals.grid_notes: Feast-guest scattering from the tables (hall floor, elev 1); already a witness to the verse — flees the blades, changes nothing about the singing.
Serving-thrall with a dropped platter, in the yard between hall and north storehouse; pathing hazard in the lanes.
Stable-boy in the south yard near the gate; if downed by a PLAYER unit in the chaos: Sung mercy_terror −4 — the feast is watching from every doorway.

objectives.primary: Escape: Grím exits by the S gate passage [13,12]-[14,13] (before it bars at turn 8) or over the E/S wall-walk lip (3h drop, fall damage, breaks pursuit).
secondary: Every player unit exits (those left behind are captured, not slain — returned at Ch2 start with a scar and a story; TUNABLE).
No feast-guest downed by your hand.
Silence the níð-singer (e6) on the way out — pure catharsis, zero mechanical mercy: the poem is already loose (C-THEME-01).

triggers.note: The hird rouses: wave 1. e8 enters at the north lane mouth [10,0].
Wave 2, through the steward's private west hall door [1,1].
Wave 3, onto the walk at its NE end [14,1].
e5 bars the S gate passage [13,12]-[14,13]: after this only the wall-drop exits remain — the altitude currency becomes the ONLY currency. UI: gate icon crossed out.
The chant stops mid-line; the aura ends. A guest finishes the stanza from memory, quietly. Nothing can unsay it (C-FRAME-02 texture — the saga will remember this night differently).
Downed player units at battle end are captured (see secondary) — this night the crown wants the wolf's whelp ALIVE. Seeds ch1-s10.
Read-only: with the wolf-blood named in verse, pursuers bark the níð's refrain as they close — the poem hunts alongside them.
Read-only variant: guards who saw the unmasking call Grím by what they saw, not by his feast-name.

designer_notes.height_gimmick: Escape spends altitude: dropping more than 1h — off the wall-walk (elev 3), off a storehouse roof (elev 3), over the palisade lip — costs fall damage (C-ELEV-01) but BREAKS PURSUIT COLD, because the hall-guards' AI will not take a drop above 1h ('a coward's leap' is beneath the hird, and beneath their Jump). The safe routes stay long: the ground-level S gate passage at [13,12]-[14,13] until it bars at turn 8, or the two slow stairs ([12,6]-[14,6] east, [5,10]-[5,12] south) up and down again. The only Ch1 map where deliberately LOSING height, and bleeding for it, is the winning move — altitude is a currency you cash out to leave.
designer_notes.witness_setup: None to manage and that is the point: the níð was recited before the whole Yule feast, so the verse already exists independent of any survivor — witness_rule is always_sung (the scripted-story-beat exception). Grím could kill every guest in the garth and the poem would still walk out the gate on a hundred remembered tongues. The three fleeing feast-guests are texture, not levers. The battle where the player learns that a WORD is a witness that cannot be cut down (C-THEME-01).
designer_notes.intent: Escape battle under pursuit, immediately after the feast-scene unmasking (ch1-s08): reach an escape edge with Grím as pursuers reinforce on a clock (turns 3/5/7) and the S gate bars at turn 8. Pursuers are aggressive and numerically endless by design — victory is exit, not extermination. Tension knife: every turn spent fighting is a turn the gate-bar clock runs down.
